name: LockBit
description: LockBit was one of the most prolific ransomware-as-a-service operations globally, responsible for thousands of attacks across critical infrastructure, manufacturing, healthcare, and government. Operating under a professional affiliate model, LockBit 3.0 introduced a bug bounty program and stealthy techniques borrowed from BlackMatter. Law enforcement disrupted LockBit infrastructure in February 2024 (Operation Cronos), but affiliates continue operating with leaked builders.

name: RansomHub
description: RansomHub emerged in February 2024 and rapidly became one of the most prolific ransomware operations, absorbing affiliates displaced by law enforcement actions against ALPHV/BlackCat and LockBit. Written in Go and C++, RansomHub targets Windows, Linux, ESXi, and NAS devices. The group uses a strict affiliate model, retaining only 10 percent of ransom payments. CISA issued an advisory in August 2024 noting over 210 victims across critical infrastructure sectors.
notable_campaigns: Change Healthcare (2024, ALPHV affiliate, RansomHub claimed data)

name: ALPHV
description: ALPHV (BlackCat) was a sophisticated RaaS operation notable for being among the first ransomware written in Rust, enabling highly customisable and cross-platform payloads targeting Windows, Linux, and VMware ESXi. The group conducted the high-profile attack on Change Healthcare in February 2024 before the FBI disrupted its infrastructure in December 2023 and again in 2024. ALPHV conducted an exit scam, retaining the $22M Change Healthcare ransom and abandoning affiliates who subsequently moved to RansomHub.

name: Cl0p
description: Cl0p (stylised Cl0p) is a prolific ransomware group closely linked to TA505/FIN11 and is known for large-scale exploitation of managed file transfer zero-days rather than traditional network intrusions. The group exploited GoAnywhere MFT (CVE-2023-0669) and MOVEit Transfer (CVE-2023-34362) in 2023, compromising hundreds of organisations in single campaigns. Cl0p frequently moves from encryption to pure data-theft extortion when encryption is not viable.

name: Black Basta
description: Black Basta emerged in April 2022 as a splinter of the Conti ransomware operation following Conti's dissolution. The group rapidly became one of the most active double-extortion operations, targeting Windows and VMware ESXi environments. Black Basta is known for purchasing access from initial access brokers, leveraging Qakbot until its disruption, and heavy use of Cobalt Strike. Internal chat logs leaked in February 2025 revealed the group's operational details and links to former Conti members. Activity significantly declined after the leak.

name: Qilin
description: Qilin (also known as Agenda) is a RaaS operation that emerged in mid-2022, written initially in Go before rewriting to Rust for improved performance and evasion. Qilin specialises in targeting VMware ESXi hypervisors, allowing rapid encryption of virtual machine infrastructure. The group gained significant attention for attacking Synnovis, a UK NHS pathology provider, in June 2024 causing widespread healthcare disruption. Affiliates can customise payloads per victim, including safe mode reboots and credential harvesting from Chrome.
notable_campaigns: Synnovis / NHS UK (2024, blood transfusion services disrupted)

name: SafePay
description: SafePay is a ransomware operation that emerged in late 2024 using a customised LockBit 3.0 (LockBit Black) builder, leveraging the leaked builder code that became public after the LockBit takedown. The group operates a data leak site and has claimed hundreds of victims since its emergence. SafePay primarily gains access via VPN credentials and RDP and is notable for relatively fast encryption times and targeting mid-market enterprises across multiple sectors. The group has been observed targeting Australian organisations.

name: Rhysida
description: Rhysida emerged in May 2023 and rapidly targeted the healthcare and education sectors. The group operates as a RaaS with a 20 percent affiliate split, offering victims a so-called cybersecurity team that will help remediate the attack for payment. Rhysida gained prominence for a major attack on the British Library in late 2023 and Insomniac Games. The FBI and CISA issued a joint advisory in November 2023. The encryptor is 64-bit PE written in C++ and uses a 4096-bit RSA key and ChaCha20.

name: BianLian
description: BianLian began as a double-extortion operation using a Go-based encryptor but pivoted in 2023 to primarily data theft and extortion without encryption, following the release of a free decryptor by Avast. The group targets critical infrastructure and professional services, gaining access predominantly via compromised RDP credentials and known vulnerabilities in public-facing applications. BianLian has targeted Australian organisations and was the subject of a joint CISA/FBI/ACSC advisory in May 2023.

name: Hunters International
description: Hunters International emerged in late 2023, reportedly acquiring the Hive ransomware codebase and infrastructure after FBI and Europol disrupted Hive in January 2023. Despite denying a direct connection, code similarities and operational overlaps strongly suggest continuity. The group operates as a RaaS with a focus on high-value targets and has shifted toward data exfiltration with or without encryption. Hunters International targets healthcare, education, and manufacturing and has a dedicated leak site listing victims.

name: Fog
description: Fog is a ransomware operation that emerged in May 2024, primarily targeting the US education sector before expanding into other verticals. The group gains initial access almost exclusively through compromised VPN credentials (SonicWall, Fortinet) and is notable for rapid time-to-ransom, often encrypting victim environments within hours of initial access. Fog uses a modified Agenda/Qilin codebase. In late 2024 Fog was observed collaborating operationally with Akira affiliates.

name: DragonForce
description: DragonForce began as a Malaysian hacktivist group before pivoting to ransomware operations in late 2023. The group gained significant attention for high-profile attacks on major UK retailers in 2025, including Marks and Spencer, Co-op, and Harrods. DragonForce operates a white-label cartel model, offering its encryptor and infrastructure to other operators. The group leverages social engineering to compromise IT help desks and identity providers, including Entra ID. Their encryptor is derived from leaked LockBit 3.0 and Conti code.
notable_campaigns: Marks and Spencer (2025, significant operational disruption)

name: 8Base
description: 8Base emerged as a prominent double-extortion group in mid-2023 despite first appearing in 2022. The group primarily uses a customised Phobos ransomware encryptor and operates a victim-shaming leak site. 8Base targets SMBs across multiple sectors and is notable for publishing large volumes of victim data simultaneously to create pressure. In February 2025, Europol and Thai police arrested four suspected 8Base members as part of a coordinated law enforcement operation.

name: Dark Angels
description: Dark Angels (operating the Dunghill Leak extortion site) is notable for targeting extremely large enterprises and demanding record ransom payments. Unlike most RaaS operators, Dark Angels conducts manual, targeted attacks rather than volume-based operations. The group allegedly received a $75 million ransom from Cencora (pharmaceutical distributor) in 2024, reported to be the largest single ransomware payment on record. Dark Angels uses multiple encryptors including customised versions of Babuk (for VMware ESXi/Linux) and Windows variants.

name: 3AM
description: 3AM is a Rust-based ransomware first observed in September 2023, used as a fallback when LockBit deployments failed. The group has operational ties to former Conti members based on infrastructure and tooling overlaps. 3AM attempts to stop security services and delete Volume Shadow Copies before encrypting files. Encrypted files receive the .threeamtime extension. The group uses a dedicated leak site and has been linked to the Conti/TrickBot ecosystem.
